en.headline: Driver charged after lorry nearly hits three schoolgirls in Tsuen Wan
en.dek: Police arrested a 43-year-old man within hours of a dashcam video showing a medium goods vehicle apparently running a red light at a pedestrian crossing on Kwok Shui Road.
body: New Territories South Regional Traffic officers said they acted after a short video circulated online showing a medium goods vehicle travelling along Kwok Shui Road in Tsuen Wan towards Shek Lei. At the signalised pedestrian crossing opposite Kwan Mun Hau Tsuen, the vehicle continued through while three schoolgirls were preparing to cross or already on the crossing.

Nobody was injured. Police treated the incident as a serious threat to the girls. After a rapid investigation the same evening, officers arrested a 43-year-old local man. He has been charged with one count of dangerous driving and is due to appear at Sha Tin Magistrates’ Courts on 25 September.

Police reiterated that dangerous driving is a serious traffic offence that can endanger other road users. The maximum penalty is three years’ imprisonment, a fine of HK$25,000 and a driving disqualification of at least six months.

zh.headline: 荃灣貨車衝燈險撞三女學生 43歲司機涉危駕被捕
zh.dek: 警方留意到網上短片後迅速調查，昨晚拘捕一名43歲本地男司機，控以一項危險駕駛罪，9月25日在沙田裁判法院提堂。
body: 新界南總區交通部表示，留意到一段網上短片，顯示一輛中型貨車沿荃灣國瑞路往石籬方向行駛，途經關門口村對開行人燈號過路處時，懷疑衝紅燈，對正在橫過該過路處的三名女學生構成嚴重威脅。
事件中沒有人受傷。警方經迅速及深入調查後，昨晚拘捕一名43歲本地男司機。他已被落案控以一項「危險駕駛」罪，將於9月25日在沙田裁判法院提堂。
警方重申，任何人在道路上危險駕駛汽車屬嚴重交通罪行，會對其他道路使用者構成危險，最高可被判監禁3年、罰款2.5萬元，以及停牌最少6個月。
